Subject: Signature authority & DocuSign routing for DPA (Finovate Labs)

Sonia — attaching our latest DPA (v3) with the changes we discussed on the call. A couple of quick logistics questions before we route for signature so procurement doesn't hit a snag: 

- Who is the authorized signatory on your side for DPAs? (Title + name, preferred email to receive the envelope)
- Do you require the envelope to be routed to anyone else for countersignature or witness (procurement, legal ops, or external counsel)?
- Any special routing order (signer order) required for DocuSign? Some customers want legal to sign first, others want procurement last.

We can send via DocuSign or AdobeSign — we prefer DocuSign for automatic status webhooks, but can do AdobeSign if that's your procurement standard.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlined.pdf (redlines inline), short summary: we accepted your retention ask in §4.2, kept subprocessors list dynamic with 30-day notice, and added the EU SCCs clause reference.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Dylan — received, and quick answers below: 

- Authority: I can sign commercial agreements up to $1M; for platform-level DPAs we need GC countersignature. Please route to me first; I will sign, then our GC (Eric Jensen) will countersign.
- Preferred emails: sonia.patel@finovate.com (me), eric.jensen@acmebank.com (GC is on a separate finance domain).
- Routing order: Sonia -> Eric (GC) -> Procurement (procurement@finovate.com) for final stamping.

We use AdobeSign internally but procurement can accept DocuSign envelopes if the envelope allows a sequential signing order. Two notes: 
1) Procurement requires a PDF/A final document for records (can you confirm you can produce that export from DocuSign?).
2) If there are any role delegations (e.g., Eric wants someone else to countersign on his behalf), we need a delegated authority email and a notarized POA on file — that slows things down.

I'll review your redlines and get back by EOD Monday.

Sonia
Sonia Patel
VP, Legal & Privacy
Finovate Labs

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@finovate.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Signature authority & DocuSign routing for DPA (Finovate Labs)

Sonia — great, thanks for the clarity. A few operational confirmations so we can build the envelope and webhook: 

- We will create the DocuSign envelope with sequential signing: Sonia (role: Signer 1) -> Eric (Signer 2) -> procurement@finovate.com (Signer 3). We can produce a PDF/A final export and attach it to the envelope.
- For GC delegation: we will allow an alternate signer to be designated, but we need the name and delegated email up front to pre-populate the envelope and avoid identity verification friction. If you anticipate delegation, please loop procurement now so we can collect any POA.
- Webhook/status: We'll provide a DocuSign status URL (see related link) and can also send final executed PDF to procurement@finovate.com automatically.

Marissa / Rishi — quick check: is there any internal policy that prevents us from setting a sequential order where the customer's legal signs before our countersign? Finovate wants to sign first; they want GC to countersign. We usually countersign last, but it's fine as long as we ensure our countersignature is an executed binding signature and not a 'final stamp' step with delays. 

Evelyn — if procurement requests a sealed PDF/A we should confirm the DocuSign export includes the audit trail and is acceptable for their records. Any objections to routing order above?

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Signature authority & DocuSign routing for DPA (Finovate Labs)

Looping in a quick operations note: we can do either order from a legal standpoint, but from a deal velocity POV preferred flow is Redwood countersign immediately after customer GC. The main friction points we've seen: 

- If the customer signs first and then assigns a delegate, DocuSign may require identity verification which can block the envelope until procurement supplies POA. So pre-populating delegate emails is best.
- PDF/A: DocuSign supports the export; we should attach both a regular PDF and the PDF/A to the final webhook payload. Ops will keep the audit log.
- Countersign timing: Redwood should countersign within 24 business hours of GC signature to avoid procurement escalation. If for any reason engineering/legal needs more time (e.g., last-minute technical annex), mark as "Pending Redwood countersign - review required" in HubSpot so the AE can track.

Rishi — can you prepare a one-paragraph internal sign-off we can paste into the envelope instructions for internal countersigners? Something that allows us to countersign on behalf of Redwood with delegated signatory authority. We should avoid attaching a separate POA if possible.

Marissa
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
